title: Prime-to-residue-characteristic uniformizer root extensions
statement: Let $R$ be a henselian discrete valuation ring [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] with fraction field $F$, algebraically closed residue field $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] of characteristic $p>0$, and uniformizer $\pi$. For every positive integer $m$ prime to $p$, all roots in a separable closure of $F$ [def-pd-separable-closure] of $X^m-1$ belong to $R$. If $\alpha^m=\pi$ in that separable closure, then the splitting field $L$ of $X^m-\pi$ is $F(\alpha)$, is cyclic Galois of degree $m$ over $F$, and has ramification index $m$ at the unique maximal ideal of the integral closure of $R$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure].

source.place: Tag 0BUB (lemma-structure-decomposition-separable-closure), final proof paragraph: splitting field of X^m minus a uniformizer and divisibility of its ramification index; for the stated henselian specialization and equality, algebra.tex Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian, simple-root lifting) and the degree bound [F(alpha):F] <= m; more-algebra.tex Tag 09E8 (remark-finite-separable-extension), the degree/ramification formula giving e <= [L:F].

proof.text: Fix $m\geq1$ prime to $p$. Its image in $k$ is nonzero, so $m$ is outside the maximal ideal of the local ring $R$ and hence a unit. Since $k$ is algebraically closed it is separably closed, and $R$ is strictly henselian by [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Apply [lem-sbc-strict-local-roots-of-unity]: $\mu_m(R)$ is cyclic of cardinality $m$. Choose a generator $\zeta$; its image in $F$ still has order $m$, since $R\hookrightarrow F$ is injective. The $m$ distinct elements of $\mu_m(R)$ remain distinct in $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$. A degree-$m$ polynomial over a field has at most $m$ roots: dividing by $X-c$ for each distinct root lowers its degree by one. Thus these already exhaust the roots of $X^m-1$ in $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$, proving the first clause.

source.place: Tags 04GF and 04GG, simple-root lifting; realized by the existing strict-local roots-of-unity lemma.

proof.text:
Put $f=X^m-\pi$ and $A=R[T]/(f)$, with $t$ the class of $T$. A uniformizer is irreducible in a DVR: if $\pi=ab$ with both factors nonunits, write $a=\pi a_1$, $b=\pi b_1$ and cancel $\pi
e0$ to get $1=\pi a_1b_1$, a contradiction. By [lem-sbc-dvr-uniformizer-root-algebra], $A$ is a DVR domain with maximal ideal $(t)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], its $R$-basis is $1,t,\ldots,t^{m-1}$. Evaluation $t\mapsto\alpha$ defines an $R$-algebra map $j:A	o F^{\mathrm{sep}}$. It is injective: in the discrete-valuation description of a DVR in [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], every nonzero $x\in A$ is $ut^r$ for a unit $u$ and $r\geq0$; $j(u)$ is a unit and $j(t)=\alpha
e0$ because $\alpha^m=\pi
e0$. Hence $j(x)
e0$. Identify $A$ with its image $R[\alpha]$.

source.place: Tag 09EV (lemma-pull-root-uniformizer), proof for the standard root algebra; includes m=1 via the cited existing node.

proof.text:
There is no nonzero $g\in F[T]$ of degree less than $m$ with $g(\alpha)=0$. Indeed write $g=\sum_{i<m}(a_i/b_i)T^i$ with $a_i,b_i\in R$ and $b_i
e0$, taking $a_i=0,b_i=1$ for absent coefficients. Put $d=\prod_{i<m}b_i
e0$. Then $dg=\sum_{i<m}a_i\prod_{j
e i}b_j\,T^i$ is a polynomial over $R$; if its evaluation is zero, injectivity in Step 2 and the basis there force every coefficient $a_i\prod_{j
e i}b_j=0$, hence every $a_i=0$, so $g=0$. If the monic degree-$m$ polynomial $f$ factored over $F$ into two positive-degree polynomials, both would have degree less than $m$, while their values at $\alpha$ multiply to zero in a field. One would vanish, contradicting what was just proved. Thus $f$ is irreducible over $F$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, degree-n assertion in the proof; explicit coefficient argument using the basis and injectivity established in Step 2.

proof.text: Take the splitting field $L\subset F^{\mathrm{sep}}$ of $f$; it contains $\alpha$ because it contains all the roots of $f$ in this fixed closure. Apply [lem-exc-kummer-binomial-splitting-field] with $K=F$, $n=m$, $a=\pi$, the primitive root $\zeta$ from Step 1 and irreducibility from Step 3. Its clauses give $L=F(\alpha)$, $L/F$ Galois, a cyclic Galois group, and $[L:F]=m$.

source.place: Tag 09I6 (section-Kummer), opening paragraph; exact field-theoretic conclusions supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: The fraction field of the embedded $A=R[\alpha]$ is $F(\alpha)=L$: both are the smallest subfield of $F^{\mathrm{sep}}$ containing $R$ and $\alpha$, since a field containing $R$ contains all ratios from $F$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] applied to the DVR $A$, it is integrally closed in $L$. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $L$. The element $\alpha$ is integral over $R$ by $\alpha^m-\pi=0$; the integral elements form a subring containing $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], so $A=R[\alpha]\subseteq B$. Conversely, every $x\in B$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $R\subseteq A$, hence is integral over $A$, and integral closedness gives $x\in A$. Thus $B=A$. In particular it has the unique maximal ideal $(\alpha)$.

source.place: Tag 09EV, proof identifying the normal standard root algebra with the integral closure.

proof.text: With $B=A$ as in Step 5, its uniformizer is $\alpha$ by Step 2, while the base uniformizer satisfies $\pi=\alpha^m$. Thus $\mathfrak m_RB=(\pi)=(\alpha^m)=\mathfrak m_B^m$. Equivalently the normalized valuation of $B$ has $v_B(\alpha)=1$ and $v_B(\pi)=m$. By the definition of the ramification index this is $e(B/R)=m$. For $m=1$, $A=R$, $\alpha=\pi$, $L=F$, and this computation gives index and degree one and the trivial cyclic Galois group, as required.

source.place: Tag 09E4 (definition-extension-discrete-valuation-rings), definition of ramification index; Tag 09EV (4).
